intro: A thousand metres up in the Taurus, on a terrace, stands Alahan Monastery, a monastery and church in Mersin province from the 5th century AD. Its east church holds a treasure: a stone drum, the best preserved of the dome experiments that came before Hagia Sophia.
history: The monastery was founded in the fifth century on a terrace a thousand metres up in the Taurus, above the Göksu valley. Picture the community that lived here: a west church, an east church, a baptistery and rock-cut monks' cells, all joined by a colonnaded walk. And the stone drum of the east church is the best preserved of the dome solutions tried before Hagia Sophia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the east church and the west church, then the baptistery, and stroll along the colonnaded walk.
facts: Did you know? The relief over the west church door shows the archangels Michael and Gabriel, with pagan figures crushed beneath their feet. And the stone dome drum of the east church is the best preserved of the solutions tried before Hagia Sophia.
outro: This brings our journey through Alahan Monastery to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
